title: RenewalRule
description: A single country x document-kind renewal rule. One file per rule, under rules/<country_code lowercased>/<document_kind>.yml. This is public-plane data: it contains no user information and is safe to serve, cache, and mirror.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the file targets. Bumped only on breaking changes.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the country whose authority issues and renews the document. NOT the country the holder currently lives in.

document_kind.description: Stable machine identifier for the document type. Closed set: extending it is a deliberate schema PR, so that the consuming app never has to guess at a kind it has no UI for.

title.description: Human name of the document as the issuing country calls it, in English. Shown as the playbook page heading.

status.description: Provenance state. 'draft' means the numbers are unconfirmed and the app must render a prominent warning. Only a human who has checked the authority's own page may set 'verified', and doing so requires verified_on and verified_by.

validity_years.description: How long a freshly issued document lasts. Optional: some documents (police certificates) have no fixed validity and are instead accepted for a period set by whoever asks for them.

window_opens_days_before.description: Earliest you may legally apply, counted in days before expiry. A rule that only permits renewal inside the final year is 365. Use a large value (e.g. 3650) where the authority sets no lower bound.

window_closes_days_before.description: Latest you may still apply as a renewal, counted in days before expiry. 0 means up to the expiry date itself. Negative means a grace period AFTER expiry during which renewal is still possible rather than a fresh application.

processing_days_domestic.description: Calendar days from submitting to holding the document, applying inside the issuing country.

processing_days_abroad.description: Calendar days when applying from outside the issuing country, via a mission. Omit only where applying from abroad is impossible; say so in notes.

buffer_days.description: Safety margin added on top of worst-case processing when computing the start-by date. Larger where the process has a step outside the applicant's control (a police report, a document couriered to a capital).

required_documents.description: What the applicant must physically bring or upload. Each entry is one item, phrased as a noun the applicant would recognise.

authority_url.description: The issuing authority's own page for this process. Must be a government domain wherever one exists; never a blog or an agent.

appointment_required.description: Whether a booked slot is needed before turning up. Where true, appointment lead time is itself part of the delay and belongs in notes.

in_person_required.description: Whether the applicant must attend in person, typically for biometrics. This is what makes renewing from abroad expensive: it forces travel to a mission.

lapse_consequence.description: What actually happens if the deadline is missed. Concrete and specific: the reason the user acts.

notes.description: Anything that changes the plan but does not fit a field: seasonal backlogs, mission-specific quirks, recent process changes.

verified_on.description: ISO date a human last checked this rule against the authority's own page. Required when status is 'verified'. Staleness is measured from here.

verified_by.description: GitHub handle of that human, so a wrong number has an owner who can be asked.

source_urls.description: Where the numbers came from. At least one required, and at least one must be an official source for a rule to reach 'verified'.

abroad_overrides.description: Per-origin differences, keyed by the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the country the applicant is applying FROM. A Nepali passport renewed from London and from Doha share a legal window but not a queue, a fee, or a mission. Each override supplies only the fields that differ; everything else falls back to the top level.

allOf.description: A verified rule must name a date and a person. Without both, 'verified' is an unfalsifiable claim.

typical.description: What most applicants experience, in calendar days.

worst_case.description: The tail the applicant must actually plan against. Reminders are computed from this, never from typical: a reminder that fires in time for the median case fails exactly the people it most needed to reach.

item.description: The thing itself, e.g. 'Previous passport, original'.

detail.description: Format constraints that trip people up: photo dimensions, notarisation, certified translation.

obtain_lead_days.description: How long this supporting document itself takes to get. The single most important field in the schema: it is what turns 'renew by March' into 'start in November', because a prerequisite with a long lead time silently extends the whole process.

optional.description: True where the item is only needed in some circumstances, described in detail.

satisfied_by.description: Where this requirement is itself another dated document in the dataset, the rule that governs it. This is what turns a list of documents into a graph: Nepal will not renew a vehicle registration without current third-party insurance, so the insurance deadline silently governs the registration deadline. Nobody tracks that by hand, and no product that stores only expiry dates can compute it.

country_code.description: Issuing country of the prerequisite document. Usually the same as the parent rule, but not necessarily — a residence permit can require a passport from elsewhere.

document_kind.description: Kind of the prerequisite document. Must resolve to a rule that exists; bin/validate rejects a dangling reference.

amount.description: Official fee for the standard service. Excludes couriers, agents, and travel.

expedited_amount.description: Fee for the fast-track service where one exists.

note.description: Anything conditional about the fee: page count, age band, payment method the authority insists on.

authority_url.description: The specific mission's page, which is what a reader in that country actually needs.

additional_documents.description: Items this origin demands on top of the base list, e.g. proof of local residence.
